# Voice Procedure
Radios carry your voice; procedure carries your meaning. Every net is shared, every second of air time is contested, and the enemy may be copying every word. Proper voice procedure keeps transmissions short, unambiguous and anonymous.
The golden rules:
- [bold]Listen before you transmit.[/bold] Never step on traffic in progress. - [bold]Think, then key up.[/bold] Know what you will say before you say it. - [bold]Callsigns only.[/bold] Never names, never ranks. The net does not know who you are — keep it that way. - [bold]Keep it short.[/bold] If it takes longer than about ten seconds, split it with BREAK. - [bold]Acknowledge everything.[/bold] An unacknowledged order does not exist.
## The Basic Call
Every transmission follows the same skeleton — [bold]them first, you second[/bold]:
[color=#3FCF8E]HAVOC 6, this is ALPHA ROMEO — message — over.[/color]
You address the station you are calling, identify yourself with THIS IS, pass your traffic, and hand the net back with OVER. The reply mirrors it:
[color=#3FCF8E]ALPHA ROMEO, this is HAVOC 6 — send it, over.[/color]
Once both stations are established on the net, you may drop to abbreviated callsigns ("ALPHA ROMEO, HAVOC 6, send it, over").
## Prowords
Prowords are standard words with fixed meanings. They exist so nobody has to guess.
[bold]Proword[/bold]
[bold]Meaning[/bold]
THIS IS
The callsign that follows is the transmitting station.
OVER
My transmission is finished; I expect a reply.
OUT
My transmission is finished; no reply expected. Never "over and out".
ROGER
I received and understood your last transmission. Says nothing about compliance.
WILCO
Understood and [bold]will comply[/bold]. Never "roger wilco" — WILCO includes ROGER.
SAY AGAIN
Repeat your last transmission. [bold]Never say "repeat"[/bold] — on a fire support net REPEAT means "fire the last mission again".
BREAK
Pause between sections of a long message, releasing the net briefly.
STAND BY / WAIT OUT
I must pause; I will call you back. Do not tie up the net waiting.
HOW COPY
Confirm you received my message. Answer GOOD COPY or SOLID COPY.
RADIO CHECK
Report my signal strength and readability. Answer LIMA CHARLIE (loud and clear) or describe the problem ("broken and distorted").
ACTUAL
The commander in person, not their radio operator. "ALPHA 6 ACTUAL" is the squad leader themself.
INTERROGATIVE
What follows is a question.
BE ADVISED
What follows is information, no action required.
CORRECTION
I made an error; the corrected version follows.
DISREGARD
Ignore my last transmission entirely.
ALL STATIONS
Net call — everyone on the net copies. Reserved for commanders and net control.
## Worked Examples
[bold]Radio check:[/bold]
[color=#3FCF8E]"HAVOC ROMEO, this is ALPHA ROMEO, radio check, over."[/color] [color=#3FCF8E]"ALPHA ROMEO, this is HAVOC ROMEO, Lima Charlie, how me? Over."[/color] [color=#3FCF8E]"Lima Charlie, out."[/color]
[bold]Contact report[/bold] — what, where, how many, what you are doing about it:
[color=#3FCF8E]"HAVOC 6, this is ALPHA 6, contact! Infantry, squad strength, east treeline grid two-four-five, engaging, over."[/color] [color=#3FCF8E]"ALPHA 6, HAVOC 6, roger. BRAVO is moving to your flank, hold your line, over."[/color] [color=#3FCF8E]"HAVOC 6, ALPHA 6, wilco, out."[/color]
[bold]Fire support request[/bold] — warn the net first, send the details when cleared:
[color=#3FCF8E]"HAVOC OPS, this is ALPHA ROMEO, fire mission, over."[/color] [color=#3FCF8E]"ALPHA ROMEO, HAVOC OPS, send it, over."[/color] [color=#3FCF8E]"Fire mission: enemy machine gun position, north ridge by the comms tower, danger close two-five-zero meters east of our smoke, request suppression, over."[/color] [color=#3FCF8E]"ALPHA ROMEO, HAVOC OPS, roger, rounds out in three-zero seconds, stand by for splash, over."[/color] [color=#3FCF8E]"HAVOC OPS, ALPHA ROMEO, splash observed, target suppressed, end of mission, out."[/color]
[bold]Casualty evacuation:[/bold]
[color=#3FCF8E]"HAVOC ROMEO, this is BRAVO ROMEO, casevac request, over."[/color] [color=#3FCF8E]"BRAVO ROMEO, HAVOC ROMEO, send it, over."[/color] [color=#3FCF8E]"Two casualties, one urgent surgical, one walking wounded. Pickup at the LZ south of the bridge, LZ is cold, marked with green smoke, over."[/color] [color=#3FCF8E]"BRAVO ROMEO, HAVOC ROMEO, good copy, bird inbound, five mikes, out."[/color]
[bold]Commander taking the handset:[/bold]
[color=#3FCF8E]"HAVOC 6, this is ALPHA 6 ACTUAL, interrogative: do we have clearance to push past phase line DODGE? Over."[/color]
## Bad Traffic
What not to sound like — every line below leaks information, wastes air time or invites confusion:
- [color=#C46A6A]"Hey uh, command, this is Private Miller, we're kinda getting shot at over here?"[/color] — name, rank, no callsigns, no location, no strength. - [color=#C46A6A]"Can you repeat that?"[/color] — you may have just re-ordered an artillery strike. - [color=#C46A6A]Thirty seconds of unbroken monologue.[/color] — nobody can acknowledge, nobody else can report contact. - [color=#C46A6A]"Roger over and out, wilco."[/color] — pick one, they contradict each other.
Brevity is armor. The enemy direction-finds long transmissions and reads careless ones — say it clean, say it once, get off the net.
